request:
"Implement User Logout (CU-AUTH-04 / HU-19) at POST /api/identity/auth/logout along with the composable JWT and RBAC middlewares (Â§11.4). Load and apply `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` and follow constitution rules:
1. Domain (`internal/domain`, stdlib only): ensure `ErrForbidden` is defined alongside `ErrInvalidToken` and `ErrInvalidCredentials`.
2. HTTP Middlewares (`internal/adapter/http/middleware.go`): implement composable `chi` middlewares `Authenticate(jwtVerifier)` (extracts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, validates signature and `exp` via `JWTProvider.Verify` with `HS256`, injects authenticated `Claims{UserID, Role}` into `r.Context()`, and rejects missing/malformed/expired tokens with `401` via `respondError`) and `RequireRole(roles...)` (returns `403` `FORBIDDEN` if the authenticated role is not allowed).
3. Database (`db/queries/refresh_tokens.sql` + `sqlc generate`): add/verify query to revoke a refresh token by `jti` scoped to `user_id` using the existing `refresh_tokens` schema.
4. SQLite Adapter (`internal/adapter/sqlite/refresh_token_store.go`): implement `RevokeByJTI(ctx, userID, jti)` ensuring a user can only revoke their own refresh token (returning `domain.ErrInvalidToken` if not found or owned by another user).
5. Use Case (`internal/usecase/logout.go`): implement `LogoutUseCase.Execute(ctx, LogoutCommand{UserID, RefreshToken}) error` verifying the incoming refresh token, checking subject ownership against `UserID`, and revoking it via `RefreshTokenRepository`.
6. HTTP, OpenAPI & Wiring: register `POST /api/identity/auth/logout` inside an `Authenticate`-protected `chi` route group, accepting `{"refreshToken": "..."}` and returning `204 No Content`; map `ErrForbidden` -> `403` (`FORBIDDEN`) and `ErrInvalidToken` -> `401` (`INVALID_TOKEN`) in `respondError`; update `contracts/identity.openapi.yaml` and `shared/contracts/identity.openapi.yaml`; wire `LogoutUseCase` and `Authenticate` in `cmd/api/main.go`.
7. Tests (stdlib `testing`): add unit tests for `LogoutUseCase` (valid revocation, invalid token, cross-user token rejection), `:memory:` SQLite integration tests for `RevokeByJTI`, and `httptest` tests covering `204`, `400`, `401` (missing/invalid bearer token and invalid refresh token), and `403` (`RequireRole`)."
expectations: revoking access tokens before expiry is out of scope
no current route needs role restriction; RequireRole is supplied and tested only
context: constraint: ErrForbidden and ErrInvalidToken already exist in internal/domain/errors.go; respondError already maps them to 403/401

FR-001.title: Sign-out ends the named session and returns 204

FR-002.title: A revoked or expired refresh token is refused with 401 INVALID_TOKEN

FR-003.title: A refresh token owned by another account is refused without touching it

FR-004.title: Protected routes require a valid access token

FR-005.title: The caller identity comes only from the validated access token

FR-006.title: Role-restricted routes refuse a wrong role with 403 FORBIDDEN

intent: Add POST /api/identity/auth/logout behind composable JWT and RBAC middlewares, ending the caller-owned session only.

decisions.decision: The caller is identified only by verified access-token claims.
decisions.why: Any caller-supplied identity would let one learner act as another.
decisions.rejected: User id from the request body

decisions.decision: Ownership is enforced in one scoped SQL revoke; foreign and missing tokens both return ErrInvalidToken.
decisions.why: One statement removes the race between reading the owner and revoking, and the identical refusal avoids an existence oracle.
decisions.rejected: FindByToken then Revoke in the use case; 403 for the foreign case

decisions.decision: An expired or already-revoked token is refused rather than treated as a successful repeat sign-out.
decisions.why: Reporting success for a token the service cannot authorise would hide a real failure.

decisions.decision: RequireRole panics at construction on an empty allow list.
decisions.why: A misconfigured route should fail at startup, not silently allow everyone.
decisions.rejected: Silently allow, or fail per request

plan.summary: Plan: bearer-only identity, owner-scoped single-statement revoke, two composable middlewares.
plan.key_finding: ErrForbidden and the 403 mapping already exist, so this feature adds middleware and a scoped revoke rather than new error plumbing.
